title: Kadane's Algorithm, maximum subarray sum
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Find the maximum sum of a contiguous subarray.
intuition: At each index ask one question: is the best subarray ending here the previous best extended by a[i], or just a[i] alone? A running prefix that has gone negative can only hurt what follows, so drop it.

approaches.title: Brute: every subarray
Optimal: Kadane's algorithm
approaches.idea: cur = max(x, cur + x); best = max(best, cur).
approaches.whyWorks: cur is exactly "max sum of a subarray ending at i", a DP recurrence whose state fits in one variable.

specialTechnique.title: Kadane as 1-D DP
specialTechnique.body: dp[i] = max(a[i], dp[i-1] + a[i]). Because dp[i] depends only on dp[i-1], the table collapses to a scalar — the standard space-optimisation move for linear DP.

edgeCases: All negatives — the answer is the largest single element, not 0
commonMistakes: Initialising best = 0, which returns 0 on all-negative input
Resetting cur to 0 instead of to a[i]
patternRecognition: "Best contiguous X" -> DP on "best ending at i"
followUps: Maximum sum with at most k elements removed
interviewInsight: The all-negative case is the standard trap. Mention it before coding and you have effectively passed.
